runs.said: The console's view-file schema reads the pull request address and check rounds from the single `deliver` workflow. On the three-stage delivery (`stage-build`, `stage-check`, `stage-host`, then `landgate`, `land`), that data lives in other runs, so the board, item page and map show no PR and no 'Checks · round N of M'. The issue asks for `change` to accept a list of `{workflow, pointer}`, with the newest non-empty value winning. It also asks for `rounds` to gain a stage form, `{workflow, round, allowance}`, where each run of the workflow is one round. The view file gets `stage-check` entries under `returns`, `approves` and `verdicts`, and the readers use whichever shape the item is on. `deliver` items must render exactly as today. The relevant code is `schemas/factory-view.ts` (`rounds` at line 285, `change` at line 325), `factory-items.ts:296-327` (which gates facts on a single workflow), and the web readers under `packages/web/src/experiments/console/factory/`. I did not run anything, so the checks and browser evidence are untested. I did not look at the web readers or the `check:factory-view` script.

Issue 125 asks the factory console to read the three-stage delivery (stage-build, stage-check, stage-host, then landgate, land and landed). It wants the PR link (`change` as a list of workflow/pointer pairs, first non-empty result wins, newest run first), a stage form of `rounds` (`{workflow, round, allowance}`, one run per round), and stage-check entries in returns, approves and verdicts. The board card, item page and map chips must read "Checks · round N of M" with M from allowance. It also asks to restore the reverted mapping from 34bb4461a and draw it on the map within the DESIGN.md rules: back-edges join the one dashed send-back lane, a skip is a bypass that crosses no card, and a self-hand-off is a lane label. Items from before 2026-11-21 must render unchanged. The project names no triage policy, so AGENTS.md was the standard. The reader and schema half and the map half are separable, so the recommendation is to split them.

Triage's reason to split does not hold in this code. `workflowReferenceIssues` in packages/workflows/src/schemas/factory-view.ts rejects a view whose `change`, `rounds`, `returns`, `approves` or `verdicts` names a workflow that no stage lists. Once a stage lists `stage-check` and the rest, `factory-view-coverage.ts` requires every hand-off the pack graph reports between listed workflows to be declared as a map arrow (`undeclared-hand-off`). Those arrows are exactly what broke the 10 map tests. So the reader half cannot point the view file at a three-stage workflow, or show a three-stage PR or round in a browser, without the mapping and the map drawing in the same change. Without them it is a layer-only slice that proves nothing anyone can see. One outcome, about m to l, and one run can deliver it.

It does everything the item asks with the engine's own records and the map's existing rules. Each extra in the other options either restates pack logic in the console or adds map machinery for a hand-off that already draws truthfully.

Two schema fields can now take a list:
- `change` accepts one source or a list of sources.
- `rounds` accepts one source or a list, each in the deliver loop form or the new stage form `{workflow, round, allowance}`.

The owner's mapping from 34bb4461a is back, and the map draws it within its rules. Lane pills are now clamped to the row, which fixes the one real drawing defect. `check:factory-view` passes against the live home, and the full web suite passes.

`deliver` items render as before, with one exception. Old items such as 111 lose their Triage "Would it be split" shadow row. The installed triage no longer has a `split` step, and putting the shadow back makes `check:factory-view` fail.
